title: Package descriptions across ecosystems — and the three catalog rules that cannot fire

census.why: PHP's manifest, read by the JSON extractor and decided by a rule.

There is NO TOML extractor. The file falls to the residual sweep, and `classify` short-circuits on `tier === 'sweep'` before `matchRules` is ever called — so `cargo.package.description` can never fire, however well-formed it is. The description is still SURFACED, which is why G1 holds and G2 fails.
Same file format, same dead rule, different ecosystem.
Read as prose, so its sites carry `path = p[n]` and `key = "p[0]"`. `docker.label` is a `keyName` matcher testing that key against `/^org\.opencontainers\.image\./`, which never matches.

expectations.find: Le noyau de l'atelier, en PHP
expectations.why: Rendered on Packagist. Cited to a rule, so the verdict is traceable.
Rendered on pub.dev, and the field pub.dev scores a package on.

expectations.find: Le noyau de l'atelier, en Rust
expectations.why: SURFACED, not claimed. `cargo.package.description` exists, cites documentation, and is unreachable — there is no TOML extractor, so the site never carries a pointer for the rule to match. The honest report is that the bytes were found and not understood; a `translate` verdict here would be a claim the engine has no grounds for. The remedy is `src/extract/toml.ts`, not a rewritten rule.

expectations.find: Un atelier de publication pour petites équipes
expectations.why: The OCI description label. Found — the whole file is read as prose — but decided by no rule, because a prose site has no key for a `keyName` matcher to test. Recall holds; traceability does not.
A version constraint one line from a field that must be translated.

knownGaps: Three catalog rules — `cargo.package.description`, `python.pyproject.description`, `docker.label` — are well-formed, cite documentation, and cannot fire in any repository. `checkCatalog` validates a rule's SHAPE and never its reachability, so nothing in the engine says so. This case is why the benchmark carries a `neverExercisedRules` ratchet: the list may only shrink, and a fourth dead rule fails the run.
`html.title` is the fourth, recorded in surfaces-web-app rather than here.
